description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

localProtections.antiDiscriminationText: Under federal law, housing and employment discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is unlawful.
localProtections.lede: Do additional legal protections exist for the LGBTQ community at the state level in New Jersey? Do source of income protections exist for me at the state level in New Jersey?
localProtections.attributionCopy: LGBTQ Legal Protections updated by Movement Advancement Project

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

description.value:
Avalon at Edgewater offers furnished and unfurnished studio, one-, two- and three- bedroom apartment homes in Bergen County. The homes feature kitchens with quartz or granite countertops, in-unit washers and dryers, walk-in closets, and views of New York City and the George Washington Bridge from select homes.

Avalon at Edgewater is located in the heart of the highly desirable Hudson River waterfront in Bergen County. Our conveniently located Edgewater apartments offer furnished and unfurnished studio, one-, two- and three- bedroom apartment homes. The homes feature modern kitchens with quartz or granite countertops, washers and dryers in every apartment, large walk-in closets, and stunning views of New York City and the George Washington Bridge from select homes. Our Furnished+ homes come outfitted with essential stylish furniture plus all utilities, including cable and WiFi, are included in your rent. The community also features brand new amenities including a 5,000 sq ft fitness center, heated outdoor pool, resident lounge, and WAG Pet Spa and Park.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

description.value:
This is a one bedroom apartment with a large living room and plenty of closet space. The apartment is 900 sq. ft. It is located in Edgewater's famous City Place that has shopping stores and restaurants at your doorstep. The apartment has Hudson river and Manhattan views from the living room and the bedroom. This is a modern built apartment in an extremely clean building. Apartment itself is well renovated and maintained with hardwood floors, stone tiles in bathroom, custom made cherry wood closets and stainless steel appliances.

NO BROKER FEE: Listed by the owner.

City Place is a great location with Bus to Manhattan practically at your doorstep. You can also take the free ferry shuttle to Port Imperial Ferry that goes to downtown or midtown Manhattan.

Newly renovated and 2 free covered parking spots.

One month advance rent and one month security deposit required to move in. Call or text for a showing.

No Broker Fees
1 month security deposit

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

WELCOME TO LIFE AT THE BROWNSTONES

Find balance in a place where old-fashioned lamps light retail-lined streets and open spaces abound in a place that embraces the best of both worlds and puts it all directly at your doorstep. Inspired by the historic brownstone neighborhoods of New York, the stately two-tone brick buildings with townhouse-style front stoops, thoroughly complemented by the steady growth of the Englewood South neighborhood, allow you to enjoy life at your own pace.

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.

localProtections.antiDiscriminationText: Under federal law, housing and employment discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity is unlawful.
localProtections.lede: Do additional legal protections exist for the LGBTQ community at the state level in New Jersey? Do source of income protections exist for me at the state level in New Jersey?
localProtections.attributionCopy: LGBTQ Legal Protections updated by Movement Advancement Project

description.text:
If local legal protections do not exist in your state, you are still protected under federal law. 

 

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) extended federal housing and employment discrimination protections to include the LGBTQ community in 2021. This makes housing and employment discrimination based on sexual  orientation and gender identity unlawful. 

 

If you believe you've experienced discrimination when searching for housing, you can contact a local fair housing organization.

body.markdown:
LGBTQ Protections

To help you understand the most current LGBTQ laws and policies at the local level, we've partnered with the Movement Advancement Project (MAP). MAP updates their database of U.S. state laws and policies related to LGBTQ protections within 24-48 hours after a law actually goes into effect, therefore their data excludes laws that have passed but aren't yet in effect. (MAP does not maintain information about LGBTQ protections in U.S. territories.) For questions about this data or to learn more, visit [www.lgbtmap.org](https://www.lgbtmap.org/) 

 

Source of income protections

Source of income laws offer protection from discrimination based on how you pay the rent, whether you use wages from your job, a housing choice voucher (commonly known as Section 8), or alternate forms of income, such as alimony or disability. The types of income sources protected vary by state and local law. The information provided does not, and is not intended to, constitute legal advice and is for informational purposes only. The information provided here may be incomplete or out-of-date; for legal advice, please consult a local attorney.
